title: Blend Modes
learning_outcomes: Describe the role of Blend Modes and recognize when it is useful.
Apply a relevant property, selector, or technique from this lesson in a small stylesheet.
Inspect the browser result and explain one behavior, limitation, or compatibility consideration.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore Blend Modes through a small CSS example, a visual guide, and one practical check. You do not need to memorize every property at once; focus on the decision the browser is making.
content.why_it_matters: Blend Modes helps you build interfaces that remain understandable, maintainable, and usable as content and viewport conditions change.

content_blocks.title: Color and visual effects
content_blocks.alt_text: Start with content contrast before adding backgrounds, overlays, or decorative effects. Labels show the concept flow.
content_blocks.caption: Use the labeled steps as a reasoning guide; detailed behavior is described in the lesson.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Visual properties control color, imagery, boundaries, and depth. Start with a readable foreground/background combination, preserve visible focus, and add effects only when they improve hierarchy rather than obscure content.

content_blocks.title: A useful way to practice
content_blocks.text: Start with one element or component. Use the concepts in this lesson—mix-blend-mode, background-blend-mode, blending colors and images—and change one declaration at a time. Compare the page before and after the change.

items.title: mix-blend-mode
items.text: Connect mix-blend-mode to the main idea in blend modes, then verify it in a minimal browser example.

items.title: background-blend-mode
items.text: Use the simplest appropriate property first, preserve readable contrast, and check the result in all relevant themes and states.

items.title: Stacking contexts and isolation
items.text: Keep text legible at default and zoomed sizes; allow long words and translated content to wrap without hiding information.

items.title: Cross-browser visual testing
items.text: Record the observation and environment, isolate the smallest cause, and repeat the same check after changing the rule.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Put this snippet in styles.css and link it from a minimal index.html file with a viewport meta tag. Add elements whose classes match the selectors, open the page in a modern browser, and inspect computed styles. This lesson editor displays the expected result as a guide; it is not a server-side arbitrary-code runner.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original CSS snippet, save the file, and repeat the test. Remove temporary debugging rules before keeping a final version.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Use the smallest valid example, prefer a readable default, and check browser behavior rather than trusting appearance alone.

content.task: Try it yourself: build a small example that demonstrates Blend Modes. Use the simplest relevant selector and one or more declarations, inspect the browser result, and explain it in your own words.

The intended element or state visibly changes when the rule applies.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to connect a visual change to its cause.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one property, save, and compare again.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the last rule always wins.
common_mistakes.why: The cascade also considers origin, importance, layers and selector specificity; scope and source order may also matter.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect matched declarations and computed styles before changing the stylesheet.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only one viewport or interaction state.
common_mistakes.why: A rule can work at one width and fail when content, focus, zoom or preferences change.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the check at narrow and wide widths and include keyboard focus or reduced-motion checks when relevant.
